front: In Aurora, each DB cluster can have {{c1::up to 15 Aurora Replicas in addition to the primary DB instance}}.
extra: The Aurora Replicas serve reads, and the primary DB instance serves writes.

front: In Aurora, the cluster volume of each DB cluster keeps {{c1::six copies}} of all your data, spread across three AZs.
extra: Aurora replicates the data, but [you only pay for one copy](../facts/aurora.md#aurora-faq-pay-for-one-copy).

front: In Aurora Global Database, AWS says a secondary Region can be promoted to read and write in {{c1::less than 1 minute}}.
extra: The user guide says the recovery time objective (RTO) can be [in the order of minutes](../facts/aurora.md#aurora-global-rto-order-of-minutes-guide).

front: In Aurora, you can set a backup retention period of {{c1::1–35 days}}.
In Aurora, I/O charges are a large share of the database bill. Which storage configuration fits?
back: Aurora I/O-Optimized. It is best at 25% or more of spend.
extra: With I/O-Optimized there are [no additional charges for read and write I/O](../facts/aurora.md#aurora-io-optimized-no-io-charges).

front: In Aurora PostgreSQL, can you backtrack a DB cluster to an earlier time?
back: No. Backtrack is an Aurora MySQL feature.
extra: [Backtrack is not available for Aurora PostgreSQL](../facts/aurora.md#aurora-backtrack-not-for-postgresql). A point-in-time restore works by [creating a new DB cluster](../facts/aurora.md#aurora-pitr-creates-new-cluster).

front: In Aurora Serverless v2, a development database is idle most of the week. How do you stop paying for its compute?
back: Set the minimum capacity to zero ACUs, so it can pause.
extra: While an instance is auto-paused, its [instance charge is zero](../facts/aurora-serverless.md#aurora-serverless-auto-pause-billing-storage-still-charged). Storage is still charged.
